The Commission vide order dated 18.1.2019 in Petition No. 121/2007,after taking into consideration the pendency of Appeals before the Hon’ble Supreme Court adjourned the said petition _sine die_ and directed that the same be revived after the disposal of Civil Appeals by the Hon’ble Supreme Court and also directed the Petitioner to separately submit its claim in the light of the APTEL’s judgments dated 22.1.2007 and 13.6.2007 alongwith the truing-up Petitions to be filed for the period 2014-19 in respect of concerned transmission assets 6. This order is issued after considering the submissions made by the Petitioner vide affidavit dated 27.9.2019; reply of the Petitioner vide affidavit dated 20.7.2020 in response to technical validation letter; the reply of UPPCL dated 27.1.2020; and the Petitioner’s rejoinder vide affidavit dated 21.8.2020 to the reply of UPPCL. 8. Having heard the representatives of the Petitioner and perused the material on record, we proceed to dispose of the petition. 10. In response, the Petitioner has submitted that it has enclosed the copy of APTEL’s judgment dated 22.1.2007 in Appeal Nos. 81of 2005, and judgements dated13.6.2007 in Appeal Nos.139 of 2006 and Others along with its rejoinder. 11. We have considered the contention of the Petitioner and UPPCL. As pointed out by UPPCL, the Petitioner should have submitted the judgements of APTEL alongwith the Petition. It is observed that the judgments of APTEL in the subject appeals are available in the public domain. Moreover, mere non-submission of the APTEL’s judgement cannot be a cause for not entertaining the instant petition. Therefore, contention of UPPCL is rejected. However, the Petitioner is directed to submit all the related information alongwith the petition in future. T he tariff for the 2001-04 and the 2004-09 tariff period is revised in the instant order based on the observations of APTEL and Hon’ble Supreme Court’s judgement. _(iv) Liabilities to meet award of arbitration or for compliance of the order or decree of a court; and_ done in the instant order. The implementation of the directions of APTEL in case of the Petitioner was kept pending in view of the Civil Appeals filed before the Hon’ble Supreme Court. Hence, taking into consideration the facts of the case and keeping in view the interest of the consumers, we are of the view that the beneficiaries should not be burdened with the carrying cost for the difference in the tariff allowed vide earlier orders and that allowed in the instant order for the 2001-04, 2004-09 and 2009-14 tariff periods. Therefore, the Petitioner will neither claim nor pay any carrying cost from/to the beneficiaries for the difference in the tariff allowed vide earlier orders and tariff allowed in the instant order. Further, the said difference in tariff shall be recovered from the beneficiaries over a period of six months from the date of issue of this order. 28. We have considered the Petitioner’s claim.
